title: Noah Plaue on Enterprise AI Adoption | Conveo
summary: Noah Plaue of NewtonX on enterprise AI adoption: organizational inertia, survey fraud, when synthetic data helps, and why campaigns need real primary data.
body_markdown:
Why does Noah Plaue say enterprise AI adoption stalls? +


He points to organizational inertia. In a CMO study NewtonX worked on, he says something like 80% of CMOs had dealt with organizational inertia or blocking. Real AI infrastructure cannot live in a silo, so one nervous team can slow the whole effort.


What does Plaue think about synthetic data in market research? +


He says there are good synthetic options and that most current ones are poor, especially for B2B, where little reliable information about buyers exists online. Synthetic output is only legitimate when strong primary research data sits behind it.


Can synthetic personas predict outlier trends? +


Plaue would not make that his first use. Predicting an outlier means asking AI for something that does not exist yet, and he suggests talking to real young consumers instead.


Are research panels dead? +


Plaue says he was being hyperbolic when he called them dead. He still sees a use for panels, depending on their quality, but warns that panel respondents are often almost the right person, which can corrupt data without showing where.


How can you judge a product quickly, according to Plaue? +


Hear the founder talk about it. He says a founder who is truly confident will openly name what the product does not do yet while showing a clear grasp of what the customer needs.
